t: Get Maximum in Generated Array: Linear Generation
o: The array builds itself: even indices copy nums[i / 2] and odd indices add neighbors nums[(i - 1) / 2] + nums[(i + 1) / 2]. For n = 7 the rules produce [0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3] whose maximum is 3, exactly as Example 1 walks through. Because every value depends only on SMALLER indices, filling left to right guarantees all prerequisites already exist. With n <= 100 there is zero performance pressure; the exercise is transcribing the recurrence faithfully and handling the n = 0 edge case where nums = [0] and no nums[1] exists.
k: Index parity drives everything: nums[2i] = nums[i] and nums[2i+1] = nums[i] + nums[i+1] collapse to formulas over i // 2.
Bottom-up generation is automatically topologically ordered — each slot only reads strictly smaller indices.
The maximum can sit anywhere: for n = 4 the array ends with a mere 1 while index 3 holds 2, so scan everything.

a.i: Allocate n + 1 slots, seed nums[0] = 0 and nums[1] = 1, apply the parity rule for indices 2..n, then take the max. One pass, no recursion, impossible to get wrong once the odd-index formula is translated into i // 2 and i // 2 + 1.
s: Seed nums[0] = 0 and nums[1] = 1, then loop i from 2 to n setting nums[i] by parity.
Return the maximum over all entries.
a.t: O(n) — one constant-time transition per index plus one linear max scan.

a.i: Translate the definition literally: gen(i) returns i for i <= 1, recurses on gen(i / 2) for even i, and on gen(i / 2) + gen(i / 2 + 1) for odd i. Memoization collapses the call tree so every index is computed once; depth is only logarithmic. Constant factors are worse than the loop, but it shows a specification-to-code mapping directly.
s: Write gen(i) with the three definitional branches.
Cache results in an array before returning.
Return the maximum of gen(i) for i in 0..n.
a.t: O(n) — memoization ensures each value is derived exactly once in O(1).
a.sp: O(n) — cache plus O(log n) recursion stack.

w: Ship the iterative version; keep recursion for demonstrating the spec mapping. Pitfalls: crashing on n = 0 when seeding nums[1] (guard it first), using nums[i/2 + 1] for even indices, and assuming the maximum is the last element. Follow-ups: compute only nums[n] via recursion without storing everything (you still touch O(n) distinct indices worst case), or maintain a running maximum while streaming generated values.
